canonical.title: Count set bit from numbers 1 to n
canonical.sourceFilePath: 06.Bit Manipulation/1. Learn Bit Manipulation/08.Count set bit from numbers 1 to n.cpp

narrative.title: Totaling the Beacon Flashes Across the Fleet
narrative.scenario: Every fleet vessel broadcasts its ID in binary beacon pulses, one pulse per set bit. Control wants the total pulse count across IDs 1 through n. Counting vessel by vessel is too slow, so dispatch exploits the block structure of binary numbers: below the highest power of two, each bit position holds a predictable share of pulses, and the remainder above it is one more block of the same shape.
narrative.outputFormat: The total number of set bits across all integers from 1 to n inclusive.

complexity.optimalTime: O(log n) — one recursive block per set bit of n

testCases.explanation: Across 1..7 every bit position below 8 turns on exactly four times: 3 * 4 = 12.

hintLevels: Level 1: Bits form repeating patterns — you can count them per position rather than per number.
Level 2: Below 2^x, each of the x positions carries 2^(x-1) set bits; from 2^x to n the top bit adds n - 2^x + 1 more.
Level 3: Recurse on n - 2^x with the same rule — each call peels the highest set bit, so only O(log n) calls run.
